name: markdown-links-as-edges
body: Markdown links between documents must become graph edges, and every link must have a representable source and target — no link is silently dropped. Under the schema a `Uses`/`UnresolvedUse` edge admits only a Function or Struct source (and, for `Uses`, a Struct target): the ingestor retains a uses edge only when the target is a Struct and the source is a Function/Struct, and an unresolved_use only when the source is a Function/Struct (src/ingest.rs:896-915) — a File is never a legal endpoint, so every link is anchored on a Struct section, never on a File. The document-root section (see markdown-sections-as-symbols) closes the two otherwise-unrepresentable cases: (a) a link in a document with no headings, or in the preamble before the first heading, originates from that document's document-root Struct; (b) an unanchored link that targets a whole document (`[x](other.md)`, no fragment) resolves to the target document's document-root Struct. A resolved link from a section (including a document-root) to another document-root or heading section is a `Uses` edge (Struct→Struct), the reference relationship between the two symbols. An internal anchor link (`[x](#heading)`) resolves to the matching heading section Struct in the same document. A link that cannot be resolved — an external URL, a relative path no scanned markdown file provides, or a fragment that matches no heading — becomes an `UnresolvedUse` edge from the originating section Struct to an `UnresolvedTarget` carrying a category (external for a URL; unknown for a dangling relative path or an unmatched fragment), never a guessed FQN. Link resolution runs against the full document set — every scanned markdown document — never only the emitted target: markdown is bound by the frontend contract (global.constraint.frontend-full-context, requirements.requirement.full-context-targeted-emission) and is not exempt from it, so under incremental emission a re-emitted .md whose links point at unchanged documents still resolves against the full context while only emission is filtered to the target set. Link path-resolution scope — whether relative link paths resolve file-relative or repo-root-relative, and how links to non-markdown files are treated (they cannot become `Uses` edges, since a `File` is not a legal `Uses` target, so they can only be unresolved) — is a plan-time choice (see the open-points note). It does not gate this requirement's AC: the AC asserts representability and never-drop — every link becomes either a `Uses` edge to a section Struct or an `UnresolvedUse` edge to an `UnresolvedTarget` with a category, and no link is dropped or guessed — so no AC outcome rests on the deferred path base. AC: a link in a no-heading document and a preamble link each yield a `Uses` edge from the document-root Struct, and a link to a scanned markdown document yields a `Uses` edge to that document's document-root Struct — no link omitted; a two-document fixture with an anchor link yields a `Uses` edge between two section Structs; an external URL, a path that matches no scanned markdown document, and an unmatched internal fragment yield `UnresolvedUse` → `UnresolvedTarget` with categories, and no fabricated edge.
